_comment: Accepted findings for check-editor-render-parity.js (CHECK A: editor-canvas desync — a destructured+written attribute never referenced in the preview JSX; CHECK B: invalid CSS keyword passthrough — a SelectControl option value not in the target CSS property's valid keyword set). Same discipline as dead-controls-baseline.json: the guard reports NET-NEW findings only (findings NOT listed here). To accept a finding, add it here with a reason; to fix one, wire the attribute into the preview / correct the SelectControl option, then delete the entry. Empty `accepted` = zero tolerance once/if this is promoted to gate — it ships advisory-only today (2026-08-13), so nothing needs baselining yet; findings are census output, not a blocking backlog. CRITICAL: never raise the baseline silently — any increase must include a written reason (see check-element-manifest-conformance.js:796-798).

_meta.dispositionVocabularyNote: Closed vocabulary: by-design (correct, will never need fixing) / accepted-debt (real gap, consciously deferred) / detector-limitation (the checker itself is wrong — flags a rule violation per THE-MIGRATION-METHOD.md:455, not a normal outcome) / blocked (waiting on something external). See .claude/parking.md P-BASELINE-DISPOSITION-VOCABULARY / .claude/LEDGER.md.

accepted.reason: Wave A1 ShadowControl redesign (2026-09-07): the resting boxShadow/boxShadowColour pair already has a canvas preview (resolveShadowPreviewComposed(), edit.js ~L339), but no SGS block canvas-previews a HOVER colour anywhere in the framework today — the editor canvas cannot simulate :hover without JS, and no shared mechanism for that exists yet. This attr existed under a different name (boxShadowHoverColour, a separate two-mount ShadowControl) before this session's rename+consolidation into one tabbed Normal/Hover mount; the underlying desync is pre-existing framework-wide debt (see sgs/product-search's 12 identical hover-colour-family findings, untouched by this session), surfaced under a new name by the rename rather than newly introduced.
